publication: Geschichte-, Geschlechts- u. Wappen-Calender ... auf das Jahr 1747
published_apparatus_reported: title copper + heraldic illustrations on 106 engraved plates
intervention: owner added over 100 named eighteenth-century aristocratic heraldic copper engravings, cut out and lightly attached to versos of existing plates
source: Richard Bertling, Genealogie und Heraldik, Geschichte, Lager-Katalog Nr. 74 (Dresden, 1912), item 951
analytical_use: Direct historical-copy evidence that a Wappenkalender could be actively enlarged into a larger armorial reference assemblage after publication.
guards: Do not treat augmented count as publisher-issued plate count.
Do not project augmentation to other 1747 copies.
Present location of the described copy remains unresolved.

publication: Der durchlauchtigen Welt zum acht und zwantzigstenmahl neu vermehrter und verbesserter Geschichts-, Geschlechts- und Wappen-Calender auf das Jahr 1750
published_apparatus_reported: engraved frontispiece; engraved medal plate; full-page engraved colour key; 108 full-page armorial copperplates with verso text; 74 numbered double leaves with 135 genealogical tables
copy_specific_finish: 108 armorial engravings described as coloured and heightened with gold and silver
binding_and_provenance: olive-green morocco with gold tooling and armorial supralibros of Maria Josepha of Saxony, Dauphine of France (1731–1767), mother of Louis XVI; catalogue cites Olivier 2526,2
intervention: numerous additional coloured coats of arms pasted onto otherwise blank pages
analytical_use: Copy-level evidence that the serial genealogical-heraldic apparatus could be converted into a bespoke expandable armorial repository in an elite courtly copy: publisher-issued plates were coloured and metal-heightened while additional heraldic images were pasted into available blank space.
guards: Do not treat pasted arms as publisher-issued apparatus.
Do not infer Maria Josepha personally directed the augmentation without further provenance evidence.
Binding/supralibros establish copy association, not the date or agent of every later insertion.
Do not use luxury colouring/metal heightening as evidence for the standard issue state.

date: modern/private rebinding date unresolved; source components eighteenth century
publication: private Sammelband combining a fragmentary Köhler calendar component with original leaves from J. F. Seyfart's Wappenbuch material of 1767 and 1768
binding_and_provenance: private modern stiff-card binding; ex libris inside cover; previous owner supplied a handwritten/pasted inventory of the volume's contents on the front flyleaf
intervention: cross-period recombination of surviving original leaves; missing portions represented by modern copied/facsimile replacement leaves
component_control: seller describes Seyfart component as second parts of the 1767 and 1768 Wappenkalender/Wappenbuch, with nos. 36-65 assigned to 1767 and 67-87 to 1768; 19 original leaves survive in this component, some carrying one armorial image and some four
source: ZVAB / Cassiodor Antiquariat current listing, private Sammelband; listing visible in search results for Geschichts-, Geschlechts- und Wappen-Calender
analytical_use: Concrete copy-level evidence that later owners could detach the serial/cumulative heraldic apparatus from its original host sequence, recombine leaves from distinct chronological components, and restore informational continuity with copied substitutes. This is a strong control for plate/text/host separation and for treating modern completeness as a copy history rather than an edition state.
guards: The seller's description of the Köhler component gives an internally contradictory ordinal/year combination ('sieben und zwantzigstenmahl' together with 1739); do not normalize that first component to a calendar year without inspecting its surviving title/content.
Do not count modern copied leaves as eighteenth-century witnesses.
Do not infer the date or identity of the private compiler from the present binding alone.
Treat the 1767/1768 assignment as seller-described component identification pending leaf-level comparison with institutional copies.

date: 1729 host; later losses/placeholders; Red Cross provenance dated 1914/1915
publication: Der durchlauchtigen Welt ... neu vermehrter und verbesserter Geschichts-, Geschlechts- und Wappen-Calender, 1729
binding_and_provenance: current physical-copy description records an ex libris 'Grosses Sterben - Neues Leben' and Red Cross Kriegshilfebüro 1914 / Kriegsfürsorgeamt 1915 provenance marks
surviving_state: frontispiece, title and preface absent; February and March portrait leaves have repaired losses; royal British, Danish and Russian-Tsar genealogical tables absent; two blank leaves are bound as placeholders; nine full-page ruler portraits and 82 full-page armorial plates remain; some blank leaves carry children's pencil scribbles
intervention: copy-specific selective loss followed by explicit blank-leaf placeholder insertion and other repairs
source: ZVAB / Krull GmbH i.L. current listing for the 1729 Wappenkalender
analytical_use: A copy-level control showing that absence in a surviving calendar can be structured rather than merely random: missing genealogical modules can be materially marked by substitute blank leaves, while other visual modules remain. It also demonstrates the need to separate present copy configuration from publisher-issued collation.
guards: The seller speculates that the missing British, Danish and Russian material may relate to First World War provenance; no causal evidence is supplied. Record wartime provenance and selective losses as separate facts and do not infer politically motivated removal.
The date and agent of the blank-placeholder insertion are unresolved.
Do not use the surviving plate count as an edition collation.
Children's pencil marks are copy history only and are not evidence for the date or cause of the earlier losses.

date: 1750 host; date of frontispiece relocation/pasting unresolved
publication: Der durchlauchtigen Welt zum acht und zwantzigstenmahl neu vermehrter und verbesserter Geschichts-, Geschlechts- und Wappen-Kalender auf das Jahr 1750
binding_and_provenance: current Klaus Schöneborn/AbeBooks physical-copy listing; heavily rubbed paper-board binding
surviving_state: seller reports approximately 95 armorial plates and approximately the same number of genealogical tables; engraved frontispiece survives
intervention: frontispiece pasted onto the front pastedown ('Frontispiz auf Vorsatzspiegel verklebt') rather than remaining a freely turning pretitular leaf
source: Klaus Schöneborn / AbeBooks inventory 31202150105, current listing for the 1750 Wappenkalender
analytical_use: Copy-level evidence that a threshold engraving could remain attached to the book while its material function changed: a mobile pretitular plate became part of the binding surface. This reinforces the corpus distinction between design identity, impression identity, original insertion sequence and later copy assembly.
guards: The seller does not date the pasting intervention or identify its agent.
Do not treat the present pastedown position as publisher-issued placement.
Approximate surviving plate/table counts are copy-state descriptions, not edition collation.
Composition family and matrix identity cannot be inferred from the textual description alone.

publication: Johann Christoph Gatterer, Handbuch der neuesten Genealogie und Heraldik, Nürnberg, Raspische Handlung, 1762
binding_and_provenance: Hans Kümmerle Antiquariat/ZVAB current physical-copy listing; described as from a Württemberg noble library; contemporary half-leather binding
published_apparatus_reported: frontispiece; Stammtafeln; Wappentafeln; 119 copperplates with coats of arms; 9 preliminary leaves and 188 pages text in seller collation
intervention: surviving copy contains underlining/marks and is accompanied by numerous partly coloured hand-drawn coats of arms, annotations, and manuscript papers explaining the arms and their origins/provenance
source: ZVAB search listing, Hans Kümmerle - Antiquariat, 1762 Handbuch der neuesten Genealogie und Heraldik
analytical_use: Strong copy-level evidence that the Handbuch could function as an extensible working information system rather than a closed reference book. Printed genealogical/heraldic apparatus was supplemented with reader-generated colour drawings, source/origin notes and loose documentary material, closely paralleling the augmentation practices already visible in 1747 and 1750 Wappenkalender copies.
guards: Seller description does not date individual annotations, drawings or inserted documents.
Do not attribute all interventions to one owner or to the eighteenth century without handwriting/paper/provenance control.
Do not merge reader-supplied drawings with publisher-issued plate counts.
Württemberg noble-library provenance establishes an ownership context, not authorship of every annotation or insert.
